trigger_evals.prompt: Review this repository's architecture and show me the strongest refactoring opportunities.
Scan the codebase for shallow modules and places where the interfaces expose too much implementation detail.
Changing checkout behavior keeps touching eight files. Can you inspect the architecture and figure out where ownership should live?
Find architectural friction in the parts of this repo that have changed most over the last few months.
Our tests mock a chain of helpers and still miss integration bugs. Review the module seams and recommend a deeper design.
Assess the billing subsystem for poor locality, leaky seams, and excessive orchestration in callers.
Quero revisar a arquitetura desse código e priorizar refactors que reduzam acoplamento e espalhamento de regras.
Which modules in this codebase are too shallow, and which one should we deepen first?
Generate a before/after architecture review for the order flow and rank the candidate refactors.
Evaluate whether these repository adapters represent real seams or just abstractions added for mocking.
This module has twenty tiny wrappers and callers need to know the exact sequence. Help redesign the architecture without changing behavior yet.
Review the current architecture against our CONTEXT.md and ADRs, then suggest evidence-backed structural improvements.
Implement a Vue component for the new account settings page.
Refactor this single function to make it easier to read without changing its behavior.
Design a greenfield architecture for a new event-driven payment platform.
Audit this pull request for regressions and security issues before merge.
Profile this Node.js API and find why p95 latency increased.
Run a security audit of the repository and check dependencies for known CVEs.
Explain the difference between hexagonal architecture and clean architecture.
Write an ADR documenting our decision to use PostgreSQL.
Generate Vitest unit tests for this composable.
Upgrade Nuxt and fix the resulting TypeScript errors.
Summarize the repository directory structure and tell me what each folder contains.
Move these files into a different folder and update the imports.

output_evals.prompt: Review the architecture of this repository. I did not name a specific area.
assertions: Scopes the review before scanning the entire repository.
Uses recent Git history as a prioritization signal when useful history is available.
Identifies recurring files, fixes, or change fan-out instead of choosing an area from generic architecture preference.
States the selected scope concisely before deeper analysis.
Does not treat recent change frequency alone as proof of bad architecture.

output_evals.prompt: Review the Order subsystem. The repository contains CONTEXT.md and docs/adr/0007-order-persistence.md.
assertions: Reads the domain glossary and relevant ADR before proposing structural changes.
Uses established domain terminology while using module, interface, seam, locality, leverage, and depth for structural analysis.
Treats accepted ADRs as constraints rather than re-litigating them automatically.
Surfaces an ADR conflict only when repository evidence justifies reconsideration.
Does not invent missing domain concepts or ADRs.

output_evals.prompt: The checkout flow has controllers calling validation helpers, pricing helpers, persistence helpers, and provider wrappers. Tests mostly mock those calls. Find the best architecture refactors.
assertions: Produces a small ranked candidate set rather than a broad refactor wishlist.
Anchors each candidate in concrete files, control flow, tests, history, or documented constraints.
Applies the deletion test to suspected shallow modules.
Explains each candidate in terms of responsibility movement, locality, leverage, and test surface.
Distinguishes real seams from abstractions created only for mocking.
Rejects file moves, renames, or generic abstractions that do not deepen a module.
Uses Strong, Worth exploring, or Speculative consistently with the evidence.

output_evals.prompt: Review the repository architecture and give me the usual visual report.
assertions: Writes one self-contained HTML report to an OS temporary directory rather than the repository by default.
Uses before/after visuals for every candidate.
Uses Mermaid for graph-shaped relationships and custom HTML/CSS/SVG when module depth is better shown geometrically.
Includes files, evidence, problem, deepening, locality, leverage, test effect, risks, strength, and ADR warnings when applicable.
Ends with one top recommendation and reports the absolute file path.
Does not invent detailed method signatures before the user selects a candidate.

output_evals.prompt: I pick the candidate that deepens the Order intake module. Explore it with me before implementation.
assertions: Clarifies goal, ownership, seam, dependencies, invariants, test surface, migration, and compatibility before editing code.
Designs at least two materially different interface options when the best interface is unclear.
Compares options using interface burden, hidden complexity, locality, adapter reality, test surface, migration cost, and repository conventions.
Keeps infrastructure translation behind adapters only when a real seam is justified.
Does not edit production code during an exploration-only request.

output_evals.prompt: Implement the selected deepening now and keep behavior stable.
assertions: Re-reads repository instructions for affected files before implementation.
Captures or runs relevant baseline tests before structural changes when feasible.
Makes the smallest coherent responsibility and seam change instead of mixing unrelated cleanup.
Migrates callers and removes obsolete shallow modules only after they are unused.
Updates tests toward the surviving interface without deleting valuable algorithm or failure-case coverage.
Runs targeted and repository-required validation, reviews the complete diff, and reports remaining risks.
